title: CheckPlan
description: How each check in a workspace is produced. Lives at vibe-checks.yaml in the workspace root. A verifier node's evidence comes from the command declared here, so weakening a check is a tracked diff rather than an argument nobody reviews.

checks.description: Keyed by the check name a graph verifier node writes. A node whose check is absent here cannot advance, which is deliberate: an unconfigured workspace must not be the most permissive one.

screen.description: How to prove an app rendered. Three independent signals: the crash buffer is empty, the expected content is in the view hierarchy, and the frame is not blank. A blank white screen fails all three, which an exit-code check cannot see.

platform.description: android drives adb; ios drives xcrun simctl, which exposes no view hierarchy, so content has to be asserted from inside the app there.

device.description: adb serial or simulator UDID. Omit when exactly one target is attached.

launch.description: Command that installs and starts the app. Without it the verifier measures whatever is already on screen.

settleSeconds.description: Wait after launch before sampling. A frame sampled during the splash screen proves nothing either way.

expectText.description: Strings that must appear in the view hierarchy. The only signal here that says anything about data rather than pixels.

expectResourceIds.description: View identifiers that must be present.

forbidText.description: Strings that must not appear. A framework error page is not an OS-level crash, so the crash buffer stays clean for a React Native redbox or a Flutter error widget; naming their text is what catches those.

allowBlank.description: Turns off the blank-frame check for a screen that is legitimately one flat colour.

checkName.description: Matches the check-name pattern in run-state.schema.json, so a plan cannot declare a name run state would refuse to store.

entry.description: One check. Must say how it is produced: a command, a set of paths, a screen spec, a self-configuring verifier, or an explicit human decision.

verifier.description: Overrides the graph node's verifier kind. `human` means no runtime verifier can produce this check and a person decides it, which is the only route by which caller-supplied evidence reaches a verifier node. `tasks`, `shipdecision`, `experiment`, `results`, `expectation`, `release`, and `bughunt` find their own input from the workspace root and the run's slug, so they need no command, path, or screen.

auto.description: How this check is produced instead on a run whose auto flag is set. Exists so a check can stay verifier: human by default while an opted-in auto run gets a real, falsifiable alternative rather than a forged human_event. See docs/auto-ship-reviews.

command.description: Executable to run. Its exit code is the evidence; output is captured but never parsed for a verdict.

runner.description: Optional sandbox.yaml runner name. When set, the command verifier wraps the command through vibe-agent sandbox. Missing sandbox.yaml fails closed.

paths.description: For the files verifier. Proves the paths exist and hold something, which is a weaker claim than most checks need.

description.description: For humans reading the plan. The runtime ignores it, and it is the right place to record why a check is declared human.

autoEntry.description: An Auto entry, one level only. Must not itself be verifier: human — a human-only fallback for a human-only check answers nothing an auto run could not already do — and must not declare its own auto entry, so the shape below deliberately omits both.
